title: Indus Valley Civilization found by railway workers
place_text: Mohenjo-daro and Harappa, Indus River, Pakistan

tellings.quote: accidental Discovery uh Railway workers building a railway line that actually led to that

plain: The great ancient cities of the Indus River in what is now Pakistan, Mohenjo-daro and Harappa, were found by accident in the 1920s by workers building a railway line. The writer Graham Hancock, who writes about lost ancient civilizations, tells it without naming a source, calling it an "accidental Discovery". He tells it to show how whole civilizations can stay unknown until chance turns them up.
